sources.entry: OpenWA ⚠ - WhatsApp API gateway exposing messaging as REST endpoints, with a web dashboard, multi-account sessions, and webhook events (alternative to WhatsApp Business API providers). (Source Code, Clients) MIT Docker

summary.one_liner: A plugin repository for OpenWA, the self-hosted WhatsApp API gateway, containing a catalog of installable extensions (auto-replies, logging, chatbot flows, AI responder, Chatwoot sync, voice transcription) plus the authoring kit and contract docs for building new ones.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is a curated catalog of 11 OpenWA plugins, each packaged as a .zip with a manifest.json and a bundled dist/index.js. Plugins react to WhatsApp events such as message:received through a typed hook system and act through permission-gated capabilities like sending messages, fetching URLs, reading engine data, and storage. Plugins are uploaded or installed from a URL, configured per session through the dashboard or REST API, and only run after an admin enables them. The README also documents the management endpoints, the IPlugin lifecycle, the manifest schema, and the constraints (JavaScript only, package size limits, sandboxed worker threads). It includes a build script (node package.mjs <plugin>) that bundles TypeScript and zips the result, plus a vendored types/openwa.d.ts file.
use_cases: Auto-reply to WhatsApp customers outside business hours
Log WhatsApp messages to a Google Sheet
Connect WhatsApp to a Chatwoot inbox for two-way support
Transcribe WhatsApp voice notes to text
Trigger REST API calls from WhatsApp commands
Translate group chat messages between languages
Deliver Supabase phone OTP codes over WhatsApp
how_to_run: Build a plugin package: node package.mjs gsheets-logger
Configure the plugin with PUT /api/plugins/:id/config using a JSON body of { "config": { ... } }
Enable the plugin with POST /api/plugins/:id/enable using an admin-scoped API key
notable: Plugins are disabled on install and only run after an admin enables them; the enable decision persists across host restarts
Per-session config overrides let one plugin run different settings for different WhatsApp sessions, with a per-plugin support table
Sandboxed worker thread per plugin, with permissions checked at each capability call and SSRF-guarded outbound HTTP
Documentation states it reflects the verified runtime rather than aspirational design docs
caveats: Plugins run as trusted code inside a worker thread that still has Node APIs, so only install plugins you trust
Requires a running OpenWA host (v0.26.0 is the verified baseline); live WhatsApp sessions and provider credentials are outside the tested scope
gsheets-logger does not support per-session config; one instance per session is needed
Some plugins are marked beta, and the README notes certain upstream design features are not implemented
